newsitem.title: USA: U.S. beef demand aided by return to big burgers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. beef demand aided by return to big burgers.

text.p: U.S. consumers are buying more big hamburgers and have turned against low fat alternatives, boosting demand for beef, a director of fast food chain Wendy's International said on Wednesday.

"Consumers have returned to buying large hamburgers and cheeseburgers. That is great news for all of us who make our living selling beef products," Wendy's Brand Marketing Director Tom Marchese told the annual convention of the National Cattlemen's Beef Association here.
"One day they (consumers) are telling us they want low fat alternatives. The next day those products are pretty much all off the menu," he said.
Marchese said Wendy's spent more than $250 million on U.S. beef in 1996 and would be "purchasing a lot more" in 1997.

He noted that Wendy's, along with competitors McDonald's and Burger King, owned by Grand Metropolitan Plc, was currently expanding rapidly. Fast food had moved from being a treat to "an absolute necessary convenience" as the American lifestyle evolved, he said.
Wendy's International plans to open 500 new restaurants in 1997, which Marchese described as "one of the biggest growth rates in our history." It currently runs nearly 5,000 restaurants.

Marchese said the success of a promotion in December 1996 was an indication of the trends towards bigger burgers. The company offered to double the beef in a burger for 89 cents and more than 11 percent of consumers took advantage of the offer.
